{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABXvB_Ow", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhBTXS8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 8, "title": "Remove the arbitrary cartridge ROM size limit and support bank-switched MegaROMs", "body": "## Problem

The browser emulator currently rejects cartridge ROMs larger than 48 KiB, even when they are legitimate MSX1 MegaROM images. The size restriction is duplicated in three places:

- `web/app.js`: `file.size > 49152` immediately rejects larger user files.
- `crates/msx-wasm/src/lib.rs`: the Wasm upload buffer is preallocated to only 49,152 bytes, and `msx_load` rejects longer input.
- `crates/msx-core/src/lib.rs`: `Machine::load_cartridge` accepts only exactly 8, 16, 32 or 48 KiB plain images, and `Hardware::read` maps only plain cartridges.

The fixed file-size cap is confusing and prevents real bank-switched games from being loaded. Simply removing the browser check would cause buffer overflows or loading errors and would not make larger ROMs executable.

## Expected outcome

**Remove the arbitrary 48 KiB maximum for cartridge ROMs throughout the browser/Wasm/Rust pipeline.** Allow locally selected cartridge ROMs to be loaded according to the available browser/Wasm memory and supported mapper format, rather than rejected based on a hard-coded small size limit. Implement the common MSX1 MegaROM bank-switching schemes needed to actually execute larger games.

ROM **file size** and ROM **hardware/mapper compatibility** are separate concerns. For an unsupported mapper or malformed ROM, give a truthful, actionable error; do not silently truncate or pretend arbitrary files are compatible. This does not imply unlimited physical memory or universal MSX software compatibility. Preserve the existing 32 KiB validation for separately loaded **system BIOS/BASIC ROMs**.

## Context and reproduction

- Repository: `takahirox/msx-rust`, branch `main`.
- Related UI redesign: #7. Coordinate file-input wording and any ROM import UI changes; do not reintroduce or prominently advertise an obsolete 8–48 KiB maximum.
- Today: opening an otherwise valid 64 KiB or 128 KiB cartridge yields "ROM too large" in `web/app.js` before the emulator can inspect the ROM, and the Rust core also rejects it.
- MSX1 has a 64 KiB CPU address space and cartridge memory banking. Large ROMs need a mapper (e.g., ASCII8, ASCII16, Konami, Konami SCC), not a larger flat CPU address space.
- Preserve existing keyboard, video, audio, Weave BASIC, local file privacy, cartridge ejection/reset, and the GitHub Pages release pipeline. Do not bundle unauthorized game, BIOS or BASIC ROMs.
- Follow the repository's Issue template and English Issue → implementation → PR → review → merge convention.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### ROM loading and mapper behavior

- [ ] Replace the fixed 49,152-byte Wasm upload buffer with a safe, size-aware transfer mechanism for cartridge ROMs. Ensure Wasm linear memory is grown/reserved **before** JavaScript creates a writable view. Handle failed allocation/oversized length without out-of-bounds writes, panic traps, unhandled exceptions, or loss of the currently running cartridge; do not add another arbitrary small cartridge size cap.
- [ ] Remove the frontend `file.size > 49152` cartridge rejection and the fixed small-size constraint in the Rust cartridge loader. Retain appropriate ROM format validation and a clear explanation for unsupported mappers, invalid image data, or genuine platform resource limits. Retain the 32 KiB requirement for user-supplied MSX1 system ROMs as a separate path.
- [ ] Keep existing plain cartridge support (8/16/32/48 KiB) and correct entry-point/header behavior. Add bank-switched MegaROM support with accurate memory reads/writes, bank selection, power-on defaults, reset behavior and slot interactions for common **ASCII8, ASCII16, Konami, and Konami SCC mapper address decoding**. If SCC audio is not implemented, clearly document that limitation rather than claim full SCC-game compatibility.
- [ ] Expose a reliable way to specify the cartridge mapper when needed (e.g. Auto plus manual options); any auto-detection must have documented behavior, tests, and a manual override for ambiguous images. Do not infer compatibility from the ROM length alone.
- [ ] Ensure replacing/ejecting ROMs and returning to built-in BASIC restore a clean mapper state. Loading a failed/incompatible ROM must preserve the previous running state and display a helpful nonfatal error.
- [ ] Support ROM images larger than 48 KiB without truncation, including representative self-authored images of 64 KiB, 128 KiB, 256 KiB and 512 KiB or larger, subject only to genuine browser/Wasm resource limits. Avoid unnecessarily duplicating very large ROM buffers where practical.

### Browser UI, docs and privacy

- [ ] Update ROM picker labels, errors, help text, and README to remove the misleading "8–48 KiB only" implication; clearly distinguish supported plain and MegaROM mapping formats from the lack of a fixed upload size restriction. Coordinate overlapping UI changes with #7.
- [ ] Continue to read user-selected ROMs locally, with no network upload, persistence, or unauthorized ROM redistribution. Validate extensions/contents safely and report unsupported or malformed images without crashing the page.
- [ ] Document supported mapper families, autodetection/selection rules, practical compatibility limits, and how to test with legally distributable fixtures.

### Automated validation

- [ ] Add Rust unit/integration tests that exercise mapper bank writes and resulting CPU reads at representative address windows, including reset/slot effects, plain ROM regression, invalid mapper/file cases, and images larger than 48 KiB.
- [ ] Add/update Playwright browser tests to import a genuinely bank-switched self-authored cartridge larger than 48 KiB using the **real file input and Wasm path**, observe its running display/behavior, switch/eject it, and verify that failed imports do not corrupt a loaded cartridge. Check that the old "too large (48 KiB)" failure is gone.
- [ ] Run and report the repository's relevant formatting, Clippy, Rust test, Wasm build, asset inventory and browser test commands; preserve GitHub Pages deployment behavior and /msx-rust/ path tests. Automated verification is the pre-merge gate; **do not block on manual play-testing of copyrighted games**.
- [ ] Keep the implementation focused on ROM loading/mappers and necessary UI integration. Do not combine unrelated hardware/BASIC expansion or a speculative all-mappers framework with this change.

## Optional validation

- After merge, the owner may try lawfully obtained large game ROMs and file separate compatibility Issues for unmapped hardware, BIOS calls, SCC audio, or game-specific errors.
- Try larger or less common mapper images, and additional browsers, if useful.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] Verify the updated GitHub Pages deployment successfully serves the ROM-loading UI and Wasm build, and that a permitted MegaROM file can be selected without an arbitrary 48 KiB rejection. Record actual deployed results. This check must **not** block AI review or merge; report any defects as follow-up Issues.
